summary: Count the commas used when writing 1..n in standard thousands formatting (n <= 10^5).
mainInsight: A number has one comma per full group of three digits beyond the first: values from 1,000 to 999,999 have 1 comma, from 1,000,000 have 2, and so on. For n < 10^6 the total is simply the count of numbers >= 1000.

promptVariants: How many commas does a number between 1,000 and 999,999 have?
When do numbers get a second comma?
cards.explanation: Each additional group of three digits adds one comma.

promptVariants: Why is the answer n - 999 for 1000 <= n < 10^6?
cards.answer: Every number from 1000 to n has exactly one comma and smaller numbers have none, so the total is n - 1000 + 1 = n - 999. For n >= 10^6 numbers from 10^6 also have a second comma, so add max(0, n - 10^6 + 1) (and similarly for 10^9, ...).
cards.explanation: The constraint n <= 10^5 makes your formula exact.
